decisions.quote:
Recently, a novel association with risk for MS of some

markers within the CBLB gene (Cas-Br-M (murine) ecotropic retroviral transforming sequence b,

3q13.11) was observed in the island population from Sardinia.[6] To assess the associated variant in an

independent sample set from the Italian mainland is cogent for several reasons.
decisions.reason: The Introduction explicitly links the Sardinian CBLB rs9657904 MS association that this study re-tests to Reference [6], which lists all 41 authors (Sanna S ... Cucca F) and 'Nat. Genet, 2010; 42:495-7'. Although the HAL author manuscript omits titles and DOIs in references 2-12, Reference [6] uniquely identifies the shipped original Sanna et al. (2010) (10.1038/ng.584). As noted in prior coding, later references to 'the Sardinian study [5]' in Results and Discussion are a citation-numbering typo for [6], not a separate original target.

decisions.quote:
The same allele (T) of rs9657904 SNP, positively associated with MS in Sardinian population, was

significantly associated with MS risk (one tailed p = 7.35 x 10-5 ), and even showed a comparable effect

size (OR = 1.31) also in the Italian mainland (Table 1).
decisions.reason: For the validated replication of Sanna et al. (2010), the authors report that the same T allele of CBLB rs9657904 is significantly positively associated with MS risk in the continental Italian cohort (one-tailed p = 7.35 x 10^-5) with a comparable effect size (OR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.14-1.52) and no HLA interaction, concluding that their data provide further evidence of MS association with CBLB.

decisions.quote:
Background The T allele of rs9657904 within the CBLB gene was recently found to be significantly

associated with multiple sclerosis (MS) in a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in Sardinia.

Objective To replicate this association in an independent population with a different genetic

background. Methods We typed the rs9657904 variant in a sample of 1435 cases and 1466 controls

from the Italian mainland.
decisions.reason: The paper collects and genotypes new data (1,435 MS cases and 1,466 controls from the Italian mainland) to re-test the previously published association between CBLB rs9657904 and multiple sclerosis reported in Sanna et al. (2010), which meets the codebook definition of a replication.
